[The review frame]{.kicker}

## What a reviewer checks

Every draft is read against the same six-part spine — the same one your A4 must let a stranger trace.

::: {.spine-rail}
[Decision]{.node} [Evidence]{.node} [Variation]{.node} [Output]{.node} [Threshold]{.node} [Action]{.node}
:::

::: {.concept-card}
[The reviewer's question]{.card-title}
Can I trace **decision → variants/scenarios → workflow → output → threshold → limit** without asking you to explain it out loud?
:::

If any link is missing, that is the fix list — not a failure.

---

## Review format

::: {.activity-card}
[Per person]{.card-title}
- **6–8 min** — draft presentation
- **4 min** — questions from the panel and room
- **2 min** — notes captured, one priority fix agreed
:::

Those not presenting are the **engaged review panel**: take notes, mark where the spine breaks, and prepare one useful question each.

---

## A three-lens panel

Not judges with scores — three reading positions, so feedback is varied rather than repetitive.

:::: {.three-step}
::: {.step-box}
[Practice lens]{.card-title}
Would this convince a studio tutor or client? Is the recommendation usable?
:::
::: {.step-box}
[Method lens]{.card-title}
Is the workflow sound? Are assumptions and limits stated?
:::
::: {.step-box}
[Communication lens]{.card-title}
Can a busy reader get the message in 30 seconds?
:::
::::

---

## Order and the waiting role

Review order is drawn at random, so no one over-prepares for a slot.

::: {.example-card}
[While others present]{.card-title}
You are not waiting your turn — you are reviewing. Note one strong move and one missing link per presenter. Those notes are your participation record.
:::

## Reconstruct your draft in four steps

**Object this week: your A4 draft package as a reviewer will meet it.**

::: {.recall-4step}
::: {.step}
**Did** What does the draft currently claim and show?
:::
::: {.step}
**Assumed** What am I assuming the reader already knows?
:::
::: {.step}
**Risk** Which link in the spine is weakest or missing?
:::
::: {.step}
**Verify** What one fix would most improve traceability?
:::
:::

::: {.grading-note}
Post your four-step under your draft. Posting + an honest reconstruction is the graded unit. Presenting is welcomed and earns credit; it is never required and never scored as performance.
:::

---

## Triage the feedback

You will get more notes than you can act on. Sort before you fix.

| Priority | Meaning | When to fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | a spine link is missing or wrong | this week |
| **Important** | credibility or clarity gap | before submission |
| **Polish** | would improve, not essential | if time allows |

::: {.warning-card}
Fix one critical item well rather than ten polish items poorly.
:::

---

## Feedback integration plan

Turn notes into a short, owned plan.

| Area | Specific issue | Fix | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content / logic | | | |
| Workflow / evidence | | | |
| Visuals / object card | | | |
| Q&A readiness | | | |

::: {.reflection-card}
The professional skill here is not perfection. It is integrating feedback quickly and deciding what to leave alone.
:::

---

## Useful review moves (collect these)

As the room presents, note the moves worth borrowing:

- clearest framing of the decision and who it is for
- most honest statement of a limitation
- cleanest single figure that carried the message
- best answer that redirected to the key point under questioning

These become shared craft, not a ranking.

If time remains, rotate through short practice corners:

:::: {.two-col}

:::
::: {.activity-card}
[Questions]{.card-title}
Rehearse acknowledging a limit, then redirecting to the key point.
:::
::: {.activity-card}
[Object card]{.card-title}
Make the recommendation and the one figure readable at a glance.
:::
::: {.activity-card}
[Audience fit]{.card-title}
A short version for a tutor, a longer one for a method reviewer.
:::
::::

## Week 10 checklist

::: {.concept-card}
[Before Week 11]{.card-title}
1. address every **critical** item from your review
2. strengthen the weakest spine link you identified
3. get the draft timing to 6–8 minutes
4. make the object card readable in 30 seconds
:::
